summary: The note outlines best practices for secure online banking in response to a reported 65% rise in cyber-attacks on financial institutions. It covers customer measures such as strong passwords, 2FA, phishing awareness, VPN use, account monitoring, device security and ongoing education. It also describes the roles of banks, such as SecureBank Corp.'s $20 million overhaul, and of law enforcement collaboration in reducing cybercrime.
one_line: Experts advise bank customers and financial institutions on best practices for online banking security amid a 65% rise in cyber-attacks.
key_facts: A September 20, 2023 report by CyberTech Financial noted a 65% increase in cyber-attacks on financial institutions over the past year.
Phishing, malware, identity theft, and data breaches remain the most prevalent threats to online banking, often disguised as innocuous emails, links or services.
Tim Harlow recommends passwords combining upper and lower case letters, numbers, and special characters, no shorter than twelve characters.
GlobalTrust made two-factor authentication (2FA) mandatory for all online banking customers as of October 1, 2023.

Janet Li of BankSecure advises never clicking unsolicited links or giving sensitive information to unverified contacts, and contacting the bank directly through established, secure channels if a message seems suspicious.
Jeffrey T. Layton of LayeredTech Security urges avoiding public Wi-Fi for banking, using a VPN that encrypts data transmission, and keeping operating systems and banking apps updated.
Sarah Jennings advises monitoring bank accounts for unauthorized transactions and contacting the bank immediately if anything looks suspicious; many banks offer free alerts for unusual activity.
David Schmidt recommends attending webinars, signing up for newsletters, and following cybersecurity news to stay informed about evolving threats.
Ingrid Wilson of TechSafeHome encourages antivirus and antimalware software and biometric authentication such as fingerprint and facial recognition on personal devices.
SecureBank Corp. recently invested $20 million in a cybersecurity overhaul with real-time threat detection systems and additional cybersecurity specialists on its IT teams.
Sophia Turner, director of the Financial Cybercrime Task Force, said on January 15, 2024 that joint efforts with banks have led to a significant decline in successful cyber-attacks.
